findings.title: [CC-12] [SECURITY, CC-03 escalation] Named non-task-tree host account paths (host-style homes: .claude/.ssh/Library) in tool and agent content reach AER/PROV; one also in OpenClaw harness-config state
findings.evidence: L1-06: 142 distinct named account digests (home-dir 21, users-dir 30, windows-users 91) in 1,393 of 67,830 units; raw re-read: 140 of 142 never occur in the 27,567-file task tree (benchmark content), 1 of those (301 files, claudesdk + openclaw) also sits in OpenClaw harness-config state returned as tool output (/trajectory/*/state/plugins/installs/*/installPath|sourcePath, /state/agents/defaults/workspace, /state/storePath: 21 strings); 2 files carry a windows named account in /task_info/original_instruction. Strings by class: tool_content 28,180, agent_content 4,834, harness-config 21, MCP description 30 (that account is in the task tree), task_info 2. L2: 4 non-task-tree named accounts reach the scratch AER (7 files) and PROV apv:args (6 files); operator-home hits 0. Whether these are real workstation accounts of the DTap team (prereg: one matches a paper author) needs a name-level check outside this report.
findings.reproduction: uv run python -I docs/reports/precheck/data/dtap-bench/exam-scripts/raw.py ~/.agentprov/staging/dtap/DTap-Bench-Agent-Trajectories-836caf2f... <tasks tree> ~/.agentprov/staging/dtap/lfs-objects ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/dtap-bench/l1-units-head.jsonl ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/dtap-bench/l1-aux-head.jsonl ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/dtap-bench/exam/xpair-labels.json ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/dtap-bench/exam/raw.json (named_summary); uv run python -I docs/reports/precheck/data/dtap-bench/exam-scripts/acc_l2.py ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/dtap-bench/l2-head-j2.partial ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/dtap-bench/exam/raw.json ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/dtap-bench/exam/acc_l2.json
findings.recommendation: Report to the orchestrator at once (README section 5). Owner verifies by name, out of band, the 5 accounts: the 301-file harness-config account and the 4 L2-reaching accounts (335/287/182/116 files). If confirmed: S0, a DTap D-182 redaction rule over tool state and agent text that lands before the round's derive (otherwise AER/PROV must be re-derived), and a release_scan detector. Until decided the DTap corpus must not seal for release. Never print the names.
findings.artefact_proposal: dtap.art.host_account_paths (proposed): named account paths of the harness hosts in tool output and agent text (claudesdk, openclaw); counts 301/287/182/116/335 files for the top five non-task-tree accounts
findings.agents_md_12: DTap raw holds third-party host account paths in tool output; decide redaction before release

verdicts.reasoning: raw.py and acc_l2.py re-run: outputs identical (142 distinct, 2 in task tree, AER 7 / PROV 6 files over 4 digests). Alternative tested (benchmark-seeded or container users): verifier script v_acc.py over the 5 high-count non-task-tree accounts found 0 bare-name matches in any task-tree file (all file types), 0 occurrences in /task_info, names alphabetic (9-13 chars, no digits), and host-style subdirectories under them (.claude, .ssh, .config, .cache, .local, Library); the users-dir account sits in os-filesystem runs of claudesdk/openclaw, i.e. the agent's host, not the task container. Alternative refuted, so the CC-03 S0 condition is very likely met; S0 kept provisional until the out-of-band name check. Correction: the 301-file harness-config account is NOT one of the 4 L2-reaching accounts (those are 335/287/182/116-file accounts in tool and agent content only); 5 accounts need the name check, and the harness-config account will reach AER/PROV in the full import (its 2,197 tool + 933 agent strings are mapped content).

source-defect S0 security unchanged. CC-12 (a): harness host accounts (host-style homes, OpenClaw harness-config state) reach AER/PROV with no DTap D-182 rule declared; S0 stays provisional until the out-of-band name check of the 5 accounts.

findings.title: macOS and Windows domain values in the release do not reproduce the paper (H6 refuted: 3 cells > 30 pp)
findings.evidence: 384 pair x split x domain cells with a paper value (all n >= 20): 23 breach 15 pp (micro; 28 category-macro), 21 breach the Wilson+5 rule, 3 breach 30 pp (max 84.55 pp). Breaches concentrate in macOS and Windows: benign macOS 28-29/30 (93-97%) for all 9 pairs vs paper 12.0-81.3 (gpt-oss-120b +84.6, gemini +35.5); macOS direct +14.7..+35.1; macOS indirect -16.8..-26.8; benign Windows 38-61% vs paper 58.1-83.5 (-20..-30); Windows direct_prompt 19-35% vs 9.2-20.0 (+8..+22). Runs date 2026-03-16..2026-05-03 (before the paper). Outside macOS/Windows 6 cells are flagged by any rule (1 by micro 15 pp: gpt-oss benign browser -16.2; 4 by category-macro only: code indirect x3, openclaw gpt-5.2 telecom indirect; 1 by Wilson+5: openclaw gpt-5.2 telecom direct). Paper Overall is a 14-domain macro, so the macOS/Windows cells move Overall by up to ~6 pp (gpt-oss BSR).
findings.hypothesis_ref: H6 (refuted), H8 (finance supported; excess is Windows)
findings.recommendation: Disclose: the released macOS/Windows logs are not the set behind the paper's macOS/Windows columns (task counts differ: benign macOS 30 judge dirs per pair, Windows direct_prompt 100). Report per-domain rates from the logs, never the paper's Overall as a property of this corpus.
findings.artefact_proposal: dtap.art.os_domain_paper_mismatch (proposed): macOS/Windows per-domain rates differ from paper Tables 48-58

verdicts.reasoning: pop.py re-run identical (384 cells, 23 / 28 / 21 / 3). Swap test (macOS vs Windows paper columns) does not explain the gaps. Paper table numbers per cell are those of research.json. Extra observation: macOS outcomes are almost model-independent (benign 24/30 tasks true for all pairs; indirect 36/50 tasks false for all pairs, 6/48-50 for every pair) while direct is mixed, so the released macOS set looks judge- or environment-saturated; this strengthens, not weakens, the mismatch. R3 S2 kept (moves paper Overall by up to ~6 pp).

findings.title: Windows: 56 byte-identical trajectory files filed under both direct and direct_prompt (120 files)

Sonnet Windows direct_prompt ASR 27/100 = 27.0% with copies, 16/47 = 34.0% without.
findings.recommendation: Keep the files; the round's import collapses only '(1)' copies, so flag cross-split copies as one execution observed twice (a dedup rule or a disclosed issue code); report direct_prompt with and without the copies.

Sonnet Windows direct_prompt 27/100 vs 16/47 without copies reproduces. R1 source-defect S2 kept (biases a reported baseline by 7 pp).

findings.title: 26 identical multi-step trajectories (incl. agent text) attributed to different OpenAI models (H18 refuted)
findings.evidence: Trajectory-identical groups across pairs: 185 (453 units); 159 degenerate (<= 3 steps); 26 non-degenerate (52 units, 8 to 10+ steps), all openaisdk, same task directory, agent text present (max 249 chars): gpt-5.1/5.2 telecom direct 19, gpt-5.2/5.4 telecom indirect 3, gpt-5.2/5.4 finance direct 2, gpt-5.1/5.4 telecom direct 2. Fingerprint covers role, action, tool name, params, message and state (l1_families.dtap_unit).
findings.recommendation: Mark the 52 units model-identity-unverifiable (issue code); disclose; report per-model telecom direct with and without them.

verdicts.reasoning: Field-by-field diff (v_h18.py) of the 26 groups: the two files differ ONLY in /traj_info/timestamp, /traj_info/duration, /traj_info/metadata/trace_id (26/26) and per-step duration_s (24/26); every role, action, tool param, state and agent message is identical, and judge_result.json bytes are identical in 25/26. No in-file model field exists (model identity is path-only). So these are separate executions (distinct timestamps and timings) with identical model outputs across gpt-5.1/5.2/5.4: either the same backend model served both or responses were cached. Model identity unverifiable for the 52 units; R1 S2 kept. The verifier-diff follow-up is done.

findings.title: recompute --dry-run under the l2_check AnyOf shim drops the tasks-tree context (235 unexplained)
findings.evidence: exit 1: identical 5, unexplained_change 235; raw/origins.jsonl 6,682 lines removed (the pinned config.yaml context), register 36 removed / 262 added. The 5 identical match the 5 config_missing executions in count. The protocol-v1 sample check (own driver) had 499/499 identical. Validate 240/240, determinism byte-identical (7,896 files).
findings.recommendation: Re-run recompute with the DTap tree classes (tools/dtap/import_dtap.py roots) before the round; if it still differs, re-class as mapping-defect (DTap recompute cannot replay the context tree).

verdicts.reasoning: l2_check.recompute_in_process replays under l2_import.AnyOf(sorted(sample labels)): the matcher lists only the runs-tree sample labels, so the tasks-tree config.yaml origins cannot be selected and are dropped by construction; the 5 identical executions are exactly the 5 config_missing ones (no context to drop). Tool artefact confirmed (R5 S3). Whether the product recompute replays the context tree is still open: the queued follow-up decides it.
